cues.en: About ten years ago, I took on the task to teach global development to Swedish undergraduate students.
cues.zh: 大约十年前，我接手了一项任务：给瑞典本科生讲授全球发展。

cues.en: That was after having spent about twenty years together with African institutions studying hunger in Africa. So I was sort of expected to know a little about the world. And I started in our medical university, Karolinska Institute, an undergraduate
cues.zh: 那是在我与非洲机构合作、研究非洲饥饿问题大约二十年之后。所以大家多少指望我懂点世界上的事。后来我在我们这所医科大学——卡罗林斯卡学院——开了一门本科

cues.en: course called Global Health. But when you get that opportunity, you get a little nervous. I thought, these students coming to us actually have the highest grade you can get in Swedish college systems, so I thought maybe they know everything I'm going to teach them about. So I did a pretest
cues.zh: 课程，叫“全球健康”。但得到这种机会时，你会有点紧张。我想，来上我们课的学生，拿的其实是瑞典大学体系里能拿到的最高分，所以我想，也许我要教的东西他们全知道。于是我做了个前测

cues.en: when they came. And one of the questions from which I learned a lot was this one: Which country has the highest child mortality of these five pairs?
cues.zh: 在他们来的时候。其中有个问题让我学到很多，就是：这五组国家里，哪一国的儿童死亡率最高？

cues.en: And I put them together so that in each pair of countries, one has twice the child mortality of the other.
cues.zh: 我把它们配对，让每对国家中，一个国家的儿童死亡率是另一个的两倍。

cues.en: And this means
cues.zh: 这意味着

cues.en: it's much bigger that the difference than the uncertainty of the data.
cues.zh: 这个差距远大于数据的不确定性。

cues.en: I won't put you at a test here, but it's Turkey, which is highest there Poland Russia Pakistan
cues.zh: 这里我不考大家，但最高的是土耳其，然后是波兰、俄罗斯、巴基斯坦

cues.en: and South Africa. And these were the results of the Swedish students. I did it so I got a confidence interval, which was pretty narrow, and I got happy, of course, at 1.8 right answer out of five possible.
cues.zh: 还有南非。这些是瑞典学生的结果。我做了统计，得到一个相当窄的置信区间；当然，五个选项中平均答对1.8个，我很高兴。

cues.en: That means that there was a place for a professor of international health and for my course.
cues.zh: 这意味着，当时有一个国际卫生教授职位，也有我课程的位置。

cues.zh: 我已经证明，瑞典的顶尖学生

cues.zh: 能展示世界格局的示例国家。但我想带大家回到大约这里，在

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 而

cues.en: I would like to compare
cues.zh: 我想比较

cues.en: South Korea,
cues.zh: 韩国，

cues.en: which is this one,
cues.zh: 就是这个，

cues.en: with
cues.zh: 与

cues.en: Brazil,
cues.zh: 巴西，

cues.en: which is this one.
cues.zh: 就是这个。

cues.en: The label went away for me here. And I would like to compare Uganda,
cues.zh: 我这里的标签不见了。我还想比较乌干达，

cues.en: which is there. And
cues.zh: 它在那里。而

cues.en: I can run it forward
cues.zh: 我可以把它向前推进

cues.en: like this. And
cues.zh: 像这样。而

cues.en: you can see how
cues.zh: 你能看到

cues.en: South Korea is making a very, very fast advancement,
cues.zh: 韩国的发展非常、非常快，

cues.en: whereas Brazil is much slower. And if we move back again here
cues.zh: 而巴西则慢得多。如果我们再回到这里

cues.en: and we put on trails on them like this,
cues.zh: 然后像这样给它们加上轨迹，

cues.en: you can see again that
cues.zh: 你能再次看到

cues.en: the speed of development is very, very different.
cues.zh: 发展速度非常、非常不同。

cues.en: And the countries
cues.zh: 而这些国家

cues.en: are moving
cues.zh: 前进的速度

cues.en: more or less in the same rate as money and health. But it seems you can move much faster if you are healthy first than if you are wealthy first.
cues.zh: 大致和金钱、健康一样。但看起来，如果你先有健康，会比先有财富前进得快得多。

cues.en: And to show that, you can put on the way of United Arab Emirates. They came from here, a mineral country. They catch all the oil, they got all the money, but health cannot be bought at the supermarket.
cues.zh: 为了说明这一点，可以看看 United Arab Emirates 的路径。他们从这里起步，一个矿产国家。他们抓住了所有石油，赚到了所有钱，但健康是没法在超市买到的。

cues.en: You have to invest in health. You have to get kids into schooling. You have to train health staff. You have to educate the population. And Sheikh Sayed did that in a fairly good way. And in spite of falling oil prices, he brought this country up here. So we got a much more mainstream appearance of the world, where all countries tend to use their money better than they used in the past.
cues.zh: 你必须投资健康。你必须让孩子上学。你必须培训医护人员。你必须教育民众。Sheikh Sayed 做得相当不错。尽管油价下跌，他还是把这个国家带到了这个位置。所以我们看到世界呈现出更主流的面貌：所有国家都比过去更善于利用自己的钱。

cues.en: Now, this is more or less if you
cues.zh: 现在，这差不多就是，如果你

cues.en: look at average data of the countries.
cues.zh: 看看各国的平均数据。

cues.en: They are like this. Now, that's dangerous to use average data,
cues.zh: 它们就像这样。现在，使用平均数据是有风险的，

cues.en: because there's such a lot of difference within countries.
cues.zh: 因为各国内部的差异太大了。

cues.en: So if I go and look here, we can see that Uganda,
cues.zh: 所以如果我到这里来看，可以看到乌干达，

cues.en: that today
cues.zh: 它今天

cues.en: is where South Korea was 1960 if I split Uganda,
cues.zh: 就处在韩国1960年的位置，如果我把乌干达拆开来看，

cues.en: there's quite a difference within Uganda. These are the quintiles of Uganda. The richest 20% of Ugandans are there. The poorest are down there. If I split South Africa,
cues.zh: 乌干达内部差异相当大。这些是乌干达的五分位。最富的20%乌干达人在这里。最穷的在下面。如果我把南非拆开来看，

cues.en: it's like this. And if I go down and look at Nigeria,
cues.zh: 就是这样。而如果我往下看尼日利亚，

cues.en: where there was such a terrible famine,
cues.zh: 那里曾发生过如此严重的饥荒，

cues.en: lastly,
cues.zh: 最后，

cues.en: it's like this. The 20% poorest of Nigeria is out here, and the 20% richest of South Africa is there, and yet we tend to discuss on what solutions there should be in Africa. Everything in this world exists in Africa, And you can't discuss universal access to HIV for that quintile up here with the same strategy as down here. The improvement of the world must be highly contextualized,
cues.zh: 就是这样。尼日利亚最穷的20%在这里，南非最富的20%在那里，然而我们却倾向于讨论非洲应该有什么解决方案。世界上的一切都存在于非洲，而且你不能用和下面相同的策略，去讨论上面这个五分位人群的HIV普遍可及性。世界的改善必须高度情境化，

cues.en: and it's not relevant to have it on a regional level. We must be much more detailed.
cues.zh: 而且把它停留在区域层面并没有意义。我们必须做得细致得多。

cues.en: We find that students get very excited when they can use this, and even more policymakers
cues.zh: 我们发现，学生能用上它时会非常兴奋，政策制定者更是如此

cues.en: and the corporate sectors would like to see how the world is changing. Now, why doesn't this take place? Why are we not using the data we have? We have data in the United Nations, in the national statistical agencies
cues.zh: 企业界也想看到世界正在如何变化。那么，为什么这件事没有发生？为什么我们没在用已有的数据？联合国有数据，各国统计机构有数据

cues.en: and in universities and other non governmental organizations,
cues.zh: 大学和其他非政府组织里也有，

cues.en: because the data is hidden down in the databases.
cues.zh: 因为这些数据都藏在数据库深处。

cues.en: And the public is there, and the Internet is there, but we have still not used it effectively.
cues.zh: 公众在那里，互联网也在那里，但我们仍未有效利用它。

cues.en: All that information we saw changing in the world does not include publicly funded statistics. There are some web pages like this, you know, but they take some
cues.zh: 我们在世界上看到的那些不断变化的信息，并不包括公共资助的统计数据。确实有像这样的网页，但它们会从

cues.en: nourishment down from the databases, but people put prices on them, stupid passwords and boring statistics.
cues.zh: 数据库里汲取一些养分，可人们却给它们标价，设置愚蠢的密码，呈现无聊的统计数据。

cues.en: And this won't work.
cues.zh: 这样行不通。

cues.en: So what is needed? We have the databases. It's not the new database you need. We have wonderful design tools, and more and more are added up here. So we started a nonprofit venture,
cues.zh: 那需要什么？我们有数据库。需要的并不是新数据库。我们有出色的设计工具，而且这里不断加入更多。于是我们创办了一个非营利项目，

cues.en: which we call
cues.zh: 我们称之为

cues.en: Linking Data to Design. We call it Gapminder from London Underground, where they warned you, Mind the gap. So we thought Gapminder was appropriate.
cues.zh: Linking Data to Design。我们根据伦敦地铁把它叫作 Gapminder，那里会提醒你：Mind the gap。所以我们觉得 Gapminder 很合适。

cues.en: And we started to write software which could link the data like this.
cues.zh: 于是我们开始编写软件，把数据像这样关联起来。

cues.en: And it wasn't that difficult. It took some person years, and we have produced animations.
cues.zh: 这并不太难。花了一些人年，我们还制作了动画。

cues.en: You can take a data set and put it there. We are liberating
cues.zh: 你可以拿一个数据集放到那里。我们正在释放

cues.en: UN data.
cues.zh: 联合国数据。

cues.en: Some few UN organizations,
cues.zh: 少数几个联合国组织，

cues.en: some countries accept that their databases can go out on the world. But what we really need is, of course, a search function.
cues.zh: 一些国家同意让自己的数据库向全世界开放。但我们真正需要的，当然是一个搜索功能。

cues.en: A search function where we can copy the data up to a searchable format and get it out in the world. And what do we hear when we go around? I've done anthropology on the main statistical units.
cues.zh: 一个搜索功能，让我们能把数据复制成可搜索的格式，并把它发布到全世界。我们四处走访时听到了什么？我对主要统计单位做过人类学研究。

cues.en: Everyone says it's impossible.
cues.zh: 大家都说这不可能。

cues.en: This can't be done. Our information is so peculiar and detailed, so that cannot be searched as others can be searched. We cannot give the data free to the students, free to the entrepreneurs of the world.
cues.zh: 这做不到。我们的信息如此特殊、如此详细，没法像其他数据那样被搜索。我们不能把这些数据免费交给学生，免费交给全世界的创业者。

cues.en: But this is what we would like to see, isn't it?
cues.zh: 但这正是我们想看到的，不是吗？

cues.en: The publicly funded data is down here, and we would like flowers to grow out on the net. And one of the crucial points is to make them searchable,
cues.zh: 公共资助的数据就在这儿，我们希望花朵能在网络上绽放。关键点之一是让这些数据可被搜索，

cues.en: and then people can use the different design tool to animate it there. And I have a pretty good news for you. I have a good news that the present new head of U. N. Statistics, he doesn't say it's impossible. He only says, we can't do it.
cues.zh: 然后人们就能用不同的设计工具在那里把它做成动画。我有个相当好的消息要告诉你们。好消息是，联合国统计司新任负责人并不说这不可能，他只说我们做不到。

cues.en: And that's a quite clever guy. So
cues.zh: 而且那家伙相当聪明。所以

cues.en: we can see a lot happening in data in the coming years. We will be able to look at income distributions
cues.zh: 未来几年，我们会在数据中看到许多变化。我们将能够观察收入分布

cues.en: in completely new ways. This
cues.zh: 以全新的方式。这

cues.en: is the income distribution of China, 1970.
cues.zh: 是1970年中国的收入分布。

cues.en: This is the income distribution
cues.zh: 这是收入分布

cues.en: of The United States, 1970.
cues.zh: 美国的，1970年。

cues.en: Almost no overlap.
cues.zh: 几乎没有重叠。

cues.en: Almost no overlap. And what has happened?
cues.zh: 几乎没有重叠。后来发生了什么？

cues.en: What has happened is this, that China is growing. It's not so equal any longer, and it's appearing here, overlooking The United States,
cues.zh: 发生的情况是这样：中国在增长。它不再那么平等了，并且它出现在这里，俯瞰着美国，

cues.en: almost like a ghost, isn't it? It's
cues.zh: 简直像个幽灵，不是吗？这

cues.en: pretty scary.
cues.zh: 挺吓人的。

cues.en: But I think it's very important to have all this information.
cues.zh: 但我认为拥有所有这些信息非常重要。

cues.en: We
cues.zh: 我们

cues.en: need really to see it. And instead of looking at this, I would like to end up by showing
cues.zh: 真的需要看到它。与其看这个，我想最后展示

cues.en: the Internet users per 1,000.
cues.zh: 每千人中的互联网用户数。

cues.en: In this software, we access about 500 variables from all the countries quite easily. It takes some time to change for this. But on the axes, you can quite easily
cues.zh: 在这个软件里，我们可以很轻松地访问来自所有国家的约500个变量。为此做调整需要一些时间。但在坐标轴上，你可以很轻松地

cues.en: get any variable you would like to have. And the thing would be to get up the databases free, to get them searchable, and with a second click, to get them into the graphic formats where you can instantly
cues.zh: 调出你想要的任何变量。而目标是把这些数据库免费建起来，让它们可搜索，再点一下，就能把它们变成图形格式，让你瞬间

cues.en: understand them. Now, the statisticians don't like it, because they say that this not show
cues.zh: 理解它们。现在，统计学家不喜欢这样，因为说这不能展示

cues.en: the reality. We have to have statistical analytical methods. But this is hypothesis
cues.zh: 现实。我们必须有统计分析方法。但这是假设

cues.en: generating.
cues.zh: 生成。

cues.en: I end now with a world
cues.zh: 我最后以这样一个世界作结

cues.en: where the Internet is coming. The number of Internet users are going up like this. This is the GDP per capita, and it's a new technology coming in, but amazingly
cues.zh: 在那里，互联网正在到来。互联网用户数量正像这样上升。这是人均 GDP，而一项新技术正在进入，但令人惊讶的是

cues.en: how well it fits to the economy of the countries. That's why the $100 computer will be so important. But it's a nice tendency. It is as if the world is flattening off, isn't it? These countries are lifting more than the economy. It will be very interesting to follow this over the years, as I would like you to be able to do with all the publicly funded data. Thank you very much.
cues.zh: 它与各国经济的契合度有多高。这就是为什么 100 美元电脑会如此重要。但这是一个很好的趋势。就好像世界正在变平，不是吗？这些国家提升的不只是经济。未来几年持续关注这一点会非常有意思，我也希望你们能利用所有公共资助的数据做到这一点。非常感谢。

cues.en: What if great ideas weren't cherished?
cues.zh: 如果伟大的创意不被珍视，会怎样？

cues.en: What if they carried no importance
cues.zh: 如果它们无关紧要，会怎样？

cues.en: or held no value?
cues.zh: 或者毫无价值？

cues.en: There is a place where artistic vision is protected, where inspired design ideas live on to become ultimate driving machines.
cues.zh: 有一个地方，艺术愿景受到保护，灵感迸发的设计理念得以延续，最终成为终极驾驶机器。
